findings.title: Two separate ID constructions must stay identical
findings.message: Disabled day buttons built from ValidateControl will fail validation if a cell has CalendarCell but ids[i] ID differs from n.ID. In legacy mode ids[i] is prefix/cell/N, but cellID is also prefix/cell/N, so OK. In non-legacy mode CalendarDayID(id, v) uses v.Format while cellID uses %04d formatting; for years < 1000 Format('2006') pads to 4 digits, so they match. However for DST-skipped days candidate fails and the cell is disabled, which is fine.
findings.suggestion: Use a single helper for both IDs to guarantee equality.
findings.evidence:
if v, ok := candidate(month.Year(), month.Month(), day); ok {
			ids[i] = CalendarDayID(id, v)

findings.title: Liveness check compares against a detached Calendar copy
findings.message: In the DateTimePicker popover the Calendar's Navigate callback only checks liveCalendar, and live() requires c.Change != nil and c.month() equal to the rendered month. After the owner navigates, old nodes are revoked, which is intended. But the Calendar built by DateTimePicker is a throwaway whose Value is p.Value, and the Navigate/Change closures refer to p, so p.Value changes while the captured Calendar still holds the old Value copy. Location changes would not be detected because the copy is never updated.
findings.suggestion: Build the liveness check against the source (picker) state, not the detached Calendar copy.
findings.evidence: return c.ID == id && !c.Disabled && c.Change != nil && c.Value.Location() == location && c.month().Equal(month)
